page: OVHcloud a100-360 is a dual-accelerator instance within the Cloud GPU family, provisioned through KVM virtualization. The configuration pairs 30 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running at a baseline clock speed of 3.0 GHz with two NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs, delivering an aggregate 160 GB of high-bandwidth VRAM across both cards. System memory is scaled to 360 GB, providing 12 GB of RAM per vCPU to facilitate large in-memory dataset staging and processing.

Local storage comprises a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD, offering rapid read and write access for local caches, working directories, and operational scratch space. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps. The server configuration does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, which requires routing or addressing provisions depending on the deployment architecture.

Resource allocation in this profile emphasizes accelerator density and memory capacity over general-purpose CPU thread counts. With 80 GB of VRAM per GPU and a high system memory-to-core ratio, the system balances host and accelerator throughput efficiently for memory-bound tasks. Storage volume is modest compared to the memory footprint, creating a tradeoff where massive multi-terabyte datasets must be streamed or mounted from external high-capacity network volumes.

The hardware configuration suits large language model training and fine-tuning, large-scale deep learning inference pipelines, molecular modeling, and parallelized scientific computing tasks requiring dense GPU memory pools.
description: OVHcloud a100-360 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud instance within the Cloud GPU family, designed for memory-intensive parallel computing and artificial intelligence workloads. Operating on KVM virtualization with an x86_64 architecture, it features 30 dedicated vCPUs clocked at 3.0 GHz alongside 360 GB of system memory, providing 12 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration is delivered by two NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs with a combined total of 160 GB of VRAM. The instance includes 500 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network interface speed of 16 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not included by default. The high proportion of system and accelerator memory makes the server suited for large language model inference, deep learning distributed training, and compute-intensive scientific simulations.
